2026-09-04 | frankb-78 (Track A) | compiler/abi.inc, compiler/cparser.inc, compiler/ir_codegen_{aarch64,arm32,riscv32}.inc, lib/crtl/src/stdarg.c | the variadic struct ABI closed on all three cross targets (2aedcd004 aarch64, a9213e770 riscv32, 96358226d arm32 + resolve). THREE TARGETS, THREE RULES, and two differ from that same target's FIXED-parameter rule: aarch64's variadic rule IS its fixed rule unchanged, HFAs included, so {double,double} stays in d0,d1 -- the widely-read opposite belief is true and it describes APPLE's variant, a received rule that is correct about a different specification; arm32 passes an aggregate by value at EVERY size with no indirect class and SPLITS it between r1-r3 and the stack; riscv32 is by value only up to 2 x XLEN and indirect above, {double,double} included, where its own fixed rule says fa0,fa1. WHY: each target got ONE oracle both halves ask, because a caller and a callee that disagree about what a slot CONTAINS do not produce a wrong value -- measured, converting only the aarch64 caller SEGFAULTS the probe. Three things worth carrying: (1) riscv32's THREE-QUARTERS-RIGHT trap -- a pointer IS the correct answer there above 8 bytes, so any probe that happened to use a larger struct measured GREEN on a broken target, with nothing wrong with its assertion or its control; collides-with-the-default living in the CORPUS a probe is drawn from. (2) riscv32 applied NO slot alignment anywhere, so v(1, 2.5, 77) packed the double into a1:a2 against clang's a2:a3 -- fixing only the record half would have left the scalar sibling wrong in the same function -- and its variadic arm carried a `not ProcExternal` gate that made the calling convention depend on whether the linker resolved the callee, which is exactly the boundary the ticket was about. (3) arm32 needed CLASSIFICATION ONLY: its cdecl path already builds one ascending block and reads r0..r3 out of it, so the split emits itself, and __pxx_va_arg_cross32's straddle arm already assembled a reg/stack-spanning argument. Two mechanisms built for other reasons turned out to be the general case, and the size of each fix bore no relation to how different its rule looked on paper. All nine placement rows verified against clang's call site with the trailing register in every row; the three wired tests are REGRESSION GUARDS AND NOT THE PROOF, because caller and callee are both pxx.
# LOGBOOK — trivial fixes made without a ticket

One line per fix that was small enough to just do. **This is not a ticket file**:
no frontmatter, no slugs, no `board-md`, nothing to resolve, nothing to link.

The rule that authorises these, including the boundary and the comment-vs-code
trap that makes it dangerous, is **"Just fix it — the trivial-fix rule" in
`CLAUDE.md`**. Read it before adding your first line. Short version: if it cannot
change behaviour and you can verify it by reading, fix it and log it here instead
of filing.

**Format** — `date | agent | file | what and WHY`:

```
- 2026-08-30 | frankA | compiler/foo.inc | dropped the NOTE about bar; the sibling it cites was corrected on 08-29, so the clause was false
```

The **why** is the part worth writing. "fixed comment" tells the next reader
nothing and defeats the point of keeping this file.

**Conventions**

- Append at the **end**. On a rebase conflict keep both lines — never drop one.
- Batch freely: ten comment fixes in a sweep is one commit and ten lines here.
- This file's job is the one thing `git log` cannot give you cheaply — the
  isolated record of **what bypassed the ticket system**, so the practice stays
  auditable. If it ever fills with entries that plainly needed tickets, the rule
  is being over-read and should be tightened.

---
